decisions.question: Do you ratify, for address_points and parcels, (1) declaring `guards.requires` only for what the write and its consumers need, and (2) pinning every FAIL check `blocking: false` at conversion (promotion is a later peel)?
decisions.recommendation: Approve both halves. Half (2) is already the load_ravines D-8 ruling (R-FJ); verify-12c held that R-FJ covers only that half here. Half (1) is the minimal-precondition form every converted INGESTOR uses; a wider guard set would be a behaviour change at conversion (Spec 123 §3.1).

decisions.question: Each entry records a legacy defect the conversion corrected inline as a declared change (Spec 122 rung (e)) rather than pinning it and fixing after (Spec 123 §3.1). Do you ratify each one individually (AP-D4, link_wsib LW-D15 dry-run write suppression restored, LH-D8 (a), LH-D11, the heritage mass-delete row, LZ-D12 thrown path, the zoning empty-base path, link_parcels THE FIX)?
decisions.recommendation: Approve per entry, NOT as a general rule. Each entry carries measured exposure and verdict/chain parity, but a general "fix inline" rule would contradict Spec 123 §3.1 / Known Failure Mode #3. Recommend one register row listing the ratified entries by id. coa COA-D3 (coa deviation 5) is an owed operator ruling and is listed for completeness only; this lane makes no recommendation on it.

decisions.question: May an INGESTOR conversion retire the legacy console progress-cadence literals (bytes window, row modulo, expected-total denominator) as dead under the whole-array acquisition, as massing, neighbourhoods and load_wsib already did under their own plan rulings?
decisions.recommendation: Approve. The literals governed only console lines of a per-row streaming loop that no longer exists; no audit row, records_meta key or verdict reads them. Sibling steps retired the same literals under operator-authorized plans (R-FX "the cadence retirement", R-FY, R-FZ), so this makes one form for the archetype instead of two step-local precedents.

decisions.question: May parcels declare `execution.txn_scope: "step"` (one all-or-nothing transaction) in place of the legacy per-1,000-row batch commits, the same widening address_points received under Fold B3?
decisions.recommendation: Approve. The library executeWrite wraps all insert batches in one step-scoped transaction, so "step" is the truth; the success path is unchanged and a mid-run failure now leaves no partial load. address_points has the identical deviation ratified (R-FT). verify-12c found parcels' own D1 orchestrator-ruled only.
